raj (acme-corp): Hey team — after our cert rotation this morning on our private ALB (VPC) some API routes are returning 502/525 to Redwood-hosted clients. Not seeing errors from our app logs. Can you help triage?
olivia (support): Sorry you're hitting this, raj. Can you paste the exact curl you're using and a snippet of the proxy logs? Also which cert rotation method did you use (portal upload / API / S3 sync)?
raj (acme-corp): Upload via API (certificate-manager upload) and triggered a rolling reload. Repro curl from our infra box:
raj (acme-corp): ```
curl -v https://internal-api.acme.local/v1/health --resolve internal-api.acme.local:443:10.0.5.12
```
raj (acme-corp): Output shows TLS handshake then ALERT: fatal: unknown CA or "sslv3 alert handshake failure"
liam (sre): Can you run an openssl s_client to dump the chain? `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername internal-api.acme.local -showcerts`
raj (acme-corp): Ran that — pasted relevant part:
raj (acme-corp): ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = internal-api.acme.local
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=internal-api.acme.local
   i:/CN=ACME-Intermediate
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
``` 
raj (acme-corp): It looks like the intermediate isn't being served — only leaf shown.
olivia (support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) confirm the uploaded bundle contains leaf + intermediate(s) concatenated; 2) check ALB/proxy config order — it must serve the fullchain (leaf then intermediate). If you used HAProxy/nginx, show `ssl_certificate` file contents (only headers/footers redacted).
kai (eng-infra): Also confirm the platform's certificate rotator didn't strip out the cross-signed intermediate on upload. I can check the rotation job logs if you give the upload audit id.
raj (acme-corp): Audit id from upload: rot-20260315-09. Proxy is an internal ALB (haproxy 2.4). Our `ssl_certificate.pem` is a symlink managed by the rotator.
maya (support-lead): Raj, can you cat the actual file the proxy reads (redact private key) and paste the top/bottom lines. Example expected order: -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- (leaf) ... -----END CERTIFICATE----- then intermediate PEM blocks.
raj (acme-corp): Here's sanitized output:
raj (acme-corp): ```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
(leaf cert blob)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
(another blob)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
raj (acme-corp): The second blob is smaller and I think it's the root, not the intermediate. Maybe the intermediate is missing.
liam (sre): If the proxy is serving leaf+root but missing intermediate, many clients (including Redwood's public clients) will not build a chain unless they have the intermediate cached. That causes verify errors or handshake failures.
olivia (support): Can you also run from a Redwood host (we can run a quick check) — @kai / @liam do you want to attempt from our side to reproduce to verify it's ALB-side and not our egress allowlist?
kai (eng-infra): I'll run an s_client from our outbound egress node and also check rotator logs for that audit id. One sec.
rotator-bot: rotator-log rot-20260315-09: uploaded bundle size=4.2kb, parsed blocks=2, certificate_order=[leaf,root], validated_chain=false, action=symlink_deploy
kai (eng-infra): Hmm bot shows certificate_order=[leaf,root] and validated_chain=false — looks like the rotator didn't find an intermediate in the uploaded bundle and therefore didn't validate. It still deployed symlink though (bad). I'll pull the original bundle stored in /var/lib/cert-uploads/rot-20260315-09.pem for inspection.
kai (eng-infra): From storage: bundle contains leaf then root. No intermediate present. That explains it.
raj (acme-corp): We did upload a bundle we thought contained intermediate — might have a packaging problem in our build pipeline that strips it. How critical is order? Should it be leaf -> intermediate -> root?
liam (sre): Yes, order matters for many proxies: fullchain should be leaf first, then intermediate(s). Root is optional to include but often harmless. Many TLS clients don't require root in chain. So correct order: leaf, intermediate(s).
olivia (support): Quick remediation options:
- Re-upload a corrected bundle with leaf + intermediate (no root) and let rotator redeploy.
- As a quick workaround, if you control client trust stores, add the intermediate locally (not ideal).
- If you need immediate rollback, point the symlink back to the previous working bundle (rotator keeps /var/lib/cert-backups). I can coordinate a rollback if you want.
raj (acme-corp): We pushed a new bundle `rot-20260315-09b` with leaf+intermediate concatenated and re-triggered the rotate API.
kai (eng-infra): Confirmed rotator-bot logs:
rotator-bot: rot-20260315-09b: parsed blocks=3, certificate_order=[leaf,intermediate,root?], validated_chain=true, action=symlink_deploy, reload=haproxy
liam (sre): After reload, I ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername internal-api.acme.local -showcerts` and now chain shows leaf + intermediate:
liam (sre): ```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=internal-api.acme.local
   i:/CN=ACME-Intermediate
 1 s:/CN=ACME-Intermediate
   i:/CN=ACME-Root
---
verify return:1
``` 
raj (acme-corp): Our curl tests from both our infra and Redwood egress pass now. Logs show 200 OK. Thank you.
olivia (support): Great! Two follow-ups for prevention:
- We should add a rotator validation failure to block symlink deploys when validated_chain=false. I'll file an infra ticket.
- Raj: add a CI check to verify bundle contains intermediate(s) — e.g. `openssl verify -CAfile <intermediate>.pem <leaf>.pem` or look for expected issuer CNs.
kai (eng-infra): Filed INF-4532: rotator must fail deploy if validation fails. Linking rot-20260315-09 incidents.
maya (support-lead): Closing loop: customer confirmed fix, root cause = build pipeline produced bundle missing intermediate so rotator deployed incomplete bundle. Action items: INF-4532 (fail-fast rotator), support playbook update for verifying bundle order, raj to add CI check. Raj — if anything else crops up ping us here. :thumbsup:
raj (acme-corp): Thanks everyone, closing from our side.
